text: Article 14: Equality before law. The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

Article 19(1): Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc. All citizens shall have the right (a) to freedom of speech and expression; (b) to assemble peaceably and without arms; (c) to form associations or unions or co-operative societies; (d) to move freely throughout the territory of India; (e) to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India; and (g) to practise any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade or business.

Article 19(2)-(6): The rights in Article 19(1) are subject to reasonable restrictions made by law in the interests of sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, and, where applicable, contempt of court, defamation, incitement to an offence, and the other grounds specified in those clauses.
Article 21: Protection of life and personal liberty. No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

Commentary on Article 21: In Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978), the Supreme Court held that the procedure under Article 21 must be fair, just, and reasonable. Later decisions have read Article 21 to include the right to privacy (K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017), the right to a speedy trial, and the right to free legal aid. This is judicial interpretation, not statute text.

Article 22: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases. (1) No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest, nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice. (2) Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest, excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate.

chapter: Part III and Part V - Remedies for Enforcement of Rights
text: Articles 32 and 226: Remedies for enforcement of rights. Article 32(1) guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III. Article 32(2) empowers the Supreme Court to issue directions, orders, or writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari. Article 226 gives High Courts a similar power to issue writs for enforcement of Part III rights and for other purposes.

Commentary on Article 32: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the heart and soul of the Constitution. This is a historical remark from the Constituent Assembly debates, not part of the constitutional text.
